$comment: AUTHORITATIVE unit-classification table for the Distractor Derivation Model (DDM). Sole normative source (with derivation_tables.json) for normalized unit classification, inference precedence, negative-admitting units, and statement inflection. Runtime files (agent-go/unit_tables_gen.go, src/unit_tables_gen.ts, functions/src/ai/unit_tables_gen.ts, client/lib/core/utils/unit_tables_gen.dart) are GENERATED from this file by scripts/gen_derivation_tables.mjs and MUST NOT be hand-edited. Inline design tables and worked examples are explanatory and non-normative; on conflict, this JSON wins (Requirements 15.1, 15.2, 15.8, 15.9). Classifications are seeded from the current agent-go/guardrails.go behavior (isYearUnit, isCountLikeUnit, DeriveOffsetsFromSurprise) but this JSON — not runtime literals or prose — is the authority.

normalization.$comment: Deterministic normalized_unit production applied BEFORE any hint validation or inference rule (Requirement 1.2). Order of operations is fixed: trim surrounding whitespace, lowercase (invariant, not locale-aware), then collapse every run of internal whitespace to a single ASCII space.

unit_classification.$comment: Direct normalized-unit -> quantity_kind lookups checked before the ordered inference rules. Keys are already-normalized units and MUST be unique (see uniqueness_constraints.exact_unit_map). Seeded from guardrails.go: isYearUnit calendar-year words, isCountLikeUnit rejected measurement units (mapped to their real domain here), and the percent set.

inference_precedence.$comment: Ordered inference rules evaluated by the Classifier ONLY when no exact classification matches (Requirements 1.5, 1.6). The FIRST matching rule wins. Percentage must precede calendar-year, bare-noun, and fallback rules (Requirement 1.7). Calendar-year requires the year_window (Requirement 1.8). Physical-measure markers (yard, bpm, calorie, …) fire before the bare-noun count default so leftover bank units like YARDS and -YARD FIELD do not classify as count. Bare discrete nouns with a non-negative integer become count (Requirement 1.9). Unmatched non-negative integer -> count, everything else -> physical_measure (Requirement 1.10). A rule whose kind has a bounded domain must state that domain in its OWN true_number_constraint rather than `any`: `percentage_marker` is `inside_percentage_domain`, so it can never emit `percentage` for a truth the kind's own bounds exclude even if the preceding `percent_out_of_domain` router's unit list drifts away from its own. The generator rejects any rule that carries `any` while emitting a kind with a hard upper ceiling, so a future bounded kind cannot reintroduce the dependency on rule order.

match.$comment: A single non-measurement noun token (optionally plural). Measurement/domain units are already captured by unit_classification.exact and by earlier rules, so a bare noun reaching here is count-like (guardrails.go isCountLikeUnit default-true branch).

fallback.$comment: Applied when no exact classification and no inference rule matches (Requirement 1.10).

calendar_year_window.$comment: Bounds for looksLikeCalendarYear in guardrails.go: an integer in [1000, 2200] is treated as a calendar year rather than a duration measured in years (Requirement 1.8). Small integers like 3 are durations, not dates. min/max are inclusive; require_integer forbids fractional years.

percentage_domain.$comment: Bounded domain of the `percentage` kind as a proportion of a whole. Consumed ONLY by the `outside_percentage_domain` inference constraint, which routes a percent-marked unit whose true number falls outside this domain to `percent_change` (an unbounded signed delta) instead of abstaining. min/max are inclusive when `inclusive` is true.

negative_admitting_units.$comment: Quantity kinds / normalized units whose true_number and candidates may be negative. Signed domains compare mathematical values, not magnitudes (design: Strategy and multi-scalar composition). Kinds absent from admitting_kinds are non-negative domains; count and percentage in particular have hard boundaries (>=0, and <=100 for percentage). Requirements 1.9, 1.10, 5.8.

statement_inflection.$comment: Data for the Statement Consistency Gate's singular/plural grammar agreement (Requirements 6.3, 6.4, 9.3). Exact value 1 is singular; all other values are plural. invariant nouns never change form; irregular nouns use an explicit plural. Regular nouns not listed use the default suffix rules. Capitalization of the source token is preserved by the runtime; entries here are lowercase canonical forms.

uniqueness_constraints.$comment: Constraints the Table_Generator MUST enforce before emitting runtime files (Requirements 15.4, 15.5). A duplicate key where uniqueness is required is a generation failure.
